title: Lesson 1.3: Wallets, keys, hardware & multisig
use: Lesson 1.3 page in the Whop course.

scenes.vo: Lesson one point three. Wallets, keys, hardware and multisig.

scenes.sub: Set up a wallet structure where one mistake can't lose everything.
scenes.vo: Set up a wallet structure where one mistake can't lose everything.
scenes.cap: Set up a wallet structure where one mistake can't lose everything.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: a website, never photograph it, never share it. No legitimate support team will ever ask for it. Compartmentalise: separate wallets by job, so a compromise only reaches one of them. Private key: the authority to sign. Whoever has it controls the funds. Seed phrase: 12–24 words that recreate your keys. Never type it into Hardware wallet: keeps keys on a separate device. Signing requires physical confirmation. Multisig: needs M of N signers (for example 2 of 3). Good for large or shared funds. Smart wallets: contract accounts that can add spending limits, recovery and batching.

scenes.title: Worked example — the 3-wallet setup
scenes.vo: Vault, Long-term holdings, Almost never. No DeFi approvals, Hardware (or multisig). Operator, Active DeFi positions, Known, verified protocols only, Hardware. Burner, Small amounts for new apps, mints, airdrops, Anything experimental, Hot wallet.

scenes.sub: Move money down the chain (vault → operator → burner) only as needed, and sweep profits back up. If the burner gets drained, you lose only the burner's balance.
scenes.vo: Move money down the chain (vault to operator to burner) only as needed, and sweep profits back up. If the burner gets drained, you lose only the burner's balance.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Seed phrase stored offline, in two separate physical places
Vault wallet has never approved a DeFi contract
Separate burner wallet for anything new
I read every signing prompt on the hardware device screen, not just the website

lines: A "support agent" in DMs needs your seed phrase to fix a stuck transaction. What do you do?
scenes.sub: Answer: Nothing. It's a scam, every time. Block and report.

lines: Why keep the vault wallet free of approvals?
scenes.sub: Answer: Approvals let contracts move your tokens. With none, a compromised protocol can't reach it.
